reason: The cited evidence shows Si addition forms M5Si3 silicides and improves room-temperature strength and plasticity in NbMoTaW, but provides no high-temperature mechanical data for Si-containing alloys and no data on TiVNbTa. The key premise that these mechanisms will improve high-temperature strength in TiVNbTa is unsupported by the cited passages.
premises: Si microalloying forms M5Si3-type silicides in refractory high-entropy alloys
M5Si3 silicides provide precipitation hardening and improve high-temperature strength
Solid solution strengthening and sluggish diffusion in RHEAs reduce strength degradation at high temperature
Si microalloying improves yield strength and plasticity in NbMoTaW-based RHEAs
The strengthening mechanisms observed in NbMoTaWSix will transfer to TiVNbTa
